item.title: Can We Prepare Children For Financial Success Before They Start Earning?
item.description: Ufuoma Paula Onephrojire on the importance of childhood financial literacy, the inspiration behind her book, Operation Viper X7: A Money Adventure , and her mission to raise a financially conscious generation. In a world where children are increasingly exposed to financial pressures, consumerism and unrealistic portrayals of wealth, teaching them how to manage money has become more important than ever. Yet, financial education remains largely absent from many children’s formative learning experiences. Following the launch of her children’s book, Operation Viper X7: A Money Adventure , economist, financial literacy advocate and author, Ufuoma Paula Onephrojire, speaks about the personal experiences that inspired the book, why financial education must begin in childhood and her vision of making financial literacy accessible to children across Nigeria and Africa. Why should financial education begin in childhood? Interviewer: Financial literacy is increasingly becoming an important conversation among adults. Why are you making a case for introducing it to children? Ufuoma Paula: I believe we have waited too long to introduce children to conversations about money. We spend years teaching them how to read, write, calculate and prepare for examinations, but how much attention do we give to preparing them to make sound financial decisions? A child can graduate with excellent grades and still have no idea how to budget, save towards a goal, distinguish between needs and wants or manage money responsibly. Financial literacy is not something people suddenly need when they get their first salary. It is a life skill that is best developed early. Children already interact with money. They receive pocket money, make spending choices, compare what they own with what their friends have and develop attitudes towards money from what they observe at home and in society. Whether we deliberately teach them or not, they are learning something about money every day. The question is whether what they are learning is preparing them for responsible financial decisions. The lessons children learn about money today can influence the financial habits, values and decisions they carry into adulthood. Those decisions will affect not only their personal wellbeing, but also their families, businesses and communities. When we raise financially informed individuals, we are contributing to a society where people are better equipped to make responsible choices, recognise opportunities and manage resources wisely. We should teach children not just how to make money someday, but how to manage resources, recognise opportunities, create value and understand that money is a tool, not a master. Ufuoma Paula: My motivation comes from personal experiences, professional exposure and a deep desire to see the next generation develop

item.title: AGN mourns Pete Edochie, describes him as ‘father figure’
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku The National President of the Actors Guild of Nigeria (AGN), Alhaji Abubakar Yakubu, has mourned veteran actor Pete Edochie, describing him as a father figure in the Nigerian entertainment industry whose legacy would endure for generations. Edochie, 79, reportedly died in the early hours of Wednesday following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. His son, Leo Pete Edochie, announced his death in an Instagram post, describing him as “our beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman.” In his tribute, Yakubu described the late actor as an all-rounder whose contributions extended beyond Nollywood to the broadcasting industry. “Pete Edochie was a man of the people, a detribalised Nigerian who spoke different languages. He lived a noble life, a dedicated Christian and a disciplinarian,” he said. He added that the actor’s death came at a time when the industry still needed his experience and contributions. “He died when the industry needed him most. But as a thorough-bred actor, he left when the ovation was loudest,” Yakubu said. Born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State, Edochie, fondly called Ebube Dike, hailed from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, Anambra State. He began his career in broadcasting in 1967 with the Eastern Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation, where he rose to become Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. He gained national prominence in the 1980s through his portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s literary classic, Things Fall Apart. The role earned him widespread recognition and helped launch a celebrated career in Nigerian cinema. Known for his deep voice, commanding delivery and rich use of proverbs, Edochie became synonymous with portrayals of kings, community leaders and family patriarchs. His notable film credits include Igodo, Rituals and Lionheart (2018), directed by Genevieve Nnaji. In recognition of his contributions to the entertainment industry, he was honoured with the Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003, the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards Industry Merit Award and several lifetime achievement honours. item.title: Taraba youths assure Tinubu of peaceful reception ahead of campaign visit
item.description: By Femi Bolaji JALINGO — Youths and supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Taraba State have assured President Bola Tinubu of a peaceful reception ahead of his anticipated campaign visit to the state for the 2027 general elections. The youths, who also declared their readiness to mobilise support for the President and other APC candidates, made the pledge during a solidarity road walk in Tella Town, Wuryo Ward, Gassol Local Government Area. They also expressed appreciation to Tinubu for appointing Taraba indigenes to strategic positions in his administration. The convener of the road walk and Senior Special Assistant to Governor Agbu Kefas on Youth Mobilisation, Hon. Acho Righteous, described the turnout as evidence of growing support for the APC and its preparedness for the 2027 elections. Righteous commended the APC National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, for strengthening the party’s national structure and advancing its unification agenda, particularly in Taraba, which recently transitioned from PDP to APC leadership. “Our National Chairman, the erudite Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, has rebuilt the party and we are solidly behind his unification agenda. “We are now on the field and mobilising our people to ensure President Bola Tinubu, Governor Agbu Kefas and all APC candidates at the state and national levels win convincingly at the polls,” he said. He also praised the APC State Chairman, Abubakar Bawa, for promoting unity and strengthening the party’s structures across the state. The Commissioner for Science and Technology, Hon. Muslim Aruwa, and an APC chieftain, Alhaji Adamu Musa, who also spoke at the event, said the road walk demonstrated the party’s determination to consolidate its grassroots support ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Pete Edochie: Nigeria has lost a voice that time will never silence — Pat Utomi
item.description: Political economist, Pat Utomi, has paid tribute to veteran Nollywood actor, Pete Edochie, describing him as a cultural institution whose legacy will endure beyond his lifetime. Utomi, in a tribute shared on his Facebook page on Wednesday, said Nigeria had lost a distinguished voice whose contributions to the country’s entertainment industry and cultural heritage would remain unforgettable. Describing Edochie as an iroko tree that had fallen, Utomi said the veteran actor’s departure was a monumental loss not only to the entertainment industry but also to generations who grew up watching his performances. “An iroko has fallen, Nigeria has lost a voice that time will never silence,” he wrote. He described Edochie as a custodian of African storytelling and a cultural institution whose commanding presence and performances had become part of Nigeria’s collective memory. Utomi particularly recalled the actor’s portrayal of Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s literary classic, Things Fall Apart, saying he brought the character to life and presented the depth and complexities of African civilisation to the world. “When Chief Pete Edochie stood before the camera as Okonkwo in Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart, he did something extraordinary. He breathed life into a literary character and gave the world a glimpse into the depth, complexity, pride and contradictions of African civilisation,” he said. According to Utomi, Edochie did not merely interpret the character but immortalised it through his performance. He noted that the actor’s distinctive voice, commanding presence and dignified approach to his craft had earned him a special place in the hearts of audiences across generations. Beyond acting, Utomi acknowledged Edochie’s contributions to Nigerian broadcasting and cinema, saying his influence extended beyond entertainment and helped shape the country’s cultural landscape. He added that although the actor’s departure marked the end of a remarkable chapter, his legacy would continue through his films, the stories passed down to younger generations and the inspiration he provided to emerging actors. Utomi also extended his condolences to Edochie’s wife, children, family, friends and colleagues, praying that God would grant them the strength to bear the loss. “May your soul find eternal rest. Rest well, EBUBEDIKE!! Nigeria will never forget your legacy, Africa will speak your name till the end of time,” he added. item.title: 10 Things to Know About Late Nollywood Veteran Pete Edochie
item.description: The Nigerian entertainment industry has been thrown into mourning following the death of veteran Nollywood actor and broadcaster, Chief Pete Edochie, who died at the age of 79 on Wednesday, November 25, 2026. Edochie, renowned for his commanding screen presence, distinctive voice and memorable portrayal of traditional rulers and family patriarchs, was one of the most recognisable figures in Nigerian cinema. Here are 10 things to know about the late actor. 1. He was born in Zaria, Kaduna State Pete Edochie was born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State, although he hailed from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, in Anambra State. He grew up in northern Nigeria before eventually establishing his roots in the southeastern part of the country. 2. He started his career as a broadcaster Before becoming a household name in Nollywood, Edochie built a career in broadcasting. He joined the Eastern Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation in 1967 as a junior programmes assistant and gradually rose through the ranks. He later became Director of Programmes at the Anambra Broadcasting Service, where he also served as Deputy Managing Director and occasionally as Acting Managing Director. 3. He became famous for playing Okonkwo in Things Fall Apart One of the defining moments of Edochie’s career was his portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s celebrated novel, Things Fall Apart . His performance as the proud and uncompromising Igbo warrior earned him widespread recognition and established him as one of Nigeria’s leading television actors. The role also attracted international attention, including coverage by the British Broadcasting Corporation. 4. He featured in over 200 screen productions Edochie went on to feature in numerous Nigerian films and television productions throughout his career. Some of his notable works include Rituals , Igodo , Billionaire’s Club , Egg of Life and Lionheart . In Genevieve Nnaji’s 2018 film Lionheart , he played Chief Ernest Obiagu. 5. He was known for his deep voice and African proverbs One of the qualities that distinguished Edochie from many actors was his commanding voice and measured delivery. He became particularly associated with characters who portrayed traditional rulers, wealthy businessmen, fathers and authoritative family patriarchs. His frequent use of African proverbs and traditional expressions also became a defining feature of his performances, earning him admiration among generations of movie lovers. 6. He received the national honour of MON In recognition of his contributions to Nigerian entertainment, Edochie received the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003. He also received the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards Industry Merit Award and a Lifetime Achievement Award at the Africa Film Academy. item.title: “We’ve lost a titan, legend, an icon,” Gov Mbah mourns Pete Edochie
item.description: Governor of Enugu State, Dr. Peter Mbah, has expressed deep grief over the passing on of one of Nollywood’s greatest, Chief Pete Edochie, describing it as the departure of a giant, icon, and patriot. Mbah further described it as a personal loss to Enugu State, recalling that although the renown thespian hailed from Nteje in Anambra State, he had unequivocally acknowledged his life-long ties with Enugu State, which he had often described as his birth place, his “first port of call,” and a home away from home. The Governor, in his personal tribute to Edochie in the early hours of Wednesday, following the announcement of the actor’s demise, aged 79, by his son, Leo Pete Edochie, further explained that the deceased was a great ambassador of Enugu State and fan of his administration. “I am deeply saddened by the passing of Chief Pete Edochie, one of Nigeria’s most iconic actors and titans, and one of the most recognisable faces of Nollywood and Africa’s creative industry across the world. “The pain of this loss is further deepened by its timing. It comes at a particularly poignant moment when Enugu, a city whose history and identity are deeply intertwined with the arts, is hosting the National Festival of Arts and Culture (NAFEST). “At a time when we are celebrating the richness of our cultural heritage and the creative talents that give it expression, we are confronted with the loss of one of its most distinguished ambassadors. It is a sobering reminder that while we celebrate the enduring power of our arts and culture, we must also mourn those who gave them life and brought them global recognition. “Pete Edochie was more than an accomplished actor; he was an institution. With his commanding screen presence, unmistakable voice, remarkable mastery of dialogue and profound understanding of his craft, he helped shape the identity of Nigerian cinema and took the stories, values and cultural expressions of our people to audiences across the world. As an illustrious son of the South East, and dating back to his role as a tragic protagonist in the dramatization of Chinua Achebe’s 1958 novel, ‘Things Fall Apart,’ Edochie eloquently interpreted the society to the world. He wore his Igbo identity with pride, bringing its language, wisdom, proverbs and rich cultural heritage to life in ways that resonated far beyond our shores. “His performances transcended entertainment, preserving aspects of our cultural heritage and inspiring generations of actors and storytellers. “His was a career defined not merely by longevity but by excellence, distinction and enduring influence and uncommon social grace. “Even as the curtain falls on this remarkable life, his legacy as a fine broadcaster, thespian, cultural ambassador, and super star will continue to live on in the countless lives he touched and the generations of performers he inspired. “Although this is a personal loss to us as Ndi Enugu, my heart, nevertheless, particularly goes out to his immediate household. item.title: Paris Club Refunds: ‘We have no hands in transaction’ – Nigeria Governors’ Forum
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA – THE Nigeria Governors’ Forum, the umbrella body of the 36 state governors has denied having transactions with regard to the N135.5 billion paid to the forum as stakeholder in the Paris Club refunds dispute. Read Also: Paris Club Refunds: Court freezes N135.5bn linked to Governors’ Forum The NGF said it did not engage any party thereto, nor held any such monies in its custody at any time. The governors made the clarification in a statement signed very late yesterday night by Director Media and Strategic Communications NGF, Yunusa Tanko Abdullahi. It was in reaction to reports on the Federal Capital Territory Court interim order freezing N135.5 billion linked to Governors’ Forum and restraining 29 banks. The Forum said: “The Nigeria Governors’ Forum (NGF) is aware of recent media reports regarding the November 19, 2026 interim order, obtained exparte, issued by the Federal High Court of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Abuja in the Paris Club refund suit filed by Dr. Ted Iseghohi-Edwards from events that happened in 2016. “Please note that this issue emanated from allegations of transactions between the plaintiff and the Association of Local Government of Nigeria, ALGON. The Nigeria Governors Forum has no hand in that transaction and did not engage any party thereto, nor held any such monies in its custody at any time. “Meanwhile, the NGF’s legal team is currently reviewing the court processes and will respond accordingly. The Forum reiterates its unwavering commitment to the rule of law, transparency and accountability.” Abuja High Court order Justice O. C. Agbaza granted the interim Mareva injunction following an ex-parte application brought by Dr. Ted Iseghohi-Edwards. The order restrained the Incorporated Trustees of the NGF from withdrawing, transferring, dissipating or otherwise dealing with the funds. The order also restrained 29 commercial banks from releasing, transferring, converting or otherwise dealing with funds belonging to the NGF within their custody. The judge further directed the banks to disclose, within 48 hours of service, whether the NGF maintains accounts containing the disputed funds. The banks are required to identify such accounts, their currencies, available balances and amounts preserved under the court’s order. The amount represents 100 million dollar, equivalent to the N135.55 billion, calculated at the exchange rate of N1,355.80 to the dollar. Justice Agbaza made the orders on November 19, following the ex parte application and submissions by the claimant’s Counsel, Emonye Adekwu, SAN, alongside Damilola Odesola, from Ade Okeaya-Inneh & Co. Law Firm. According to the report, Iseghohi-Edwards, who carries on business as Edwards and Partners Law Firm, had sought the recovery of the money pursuant to an indemnity issued by the NGF. item.title: Emir of Daura suspended
item.description: The Katsina State Government has suspended the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Umar Farouk Umar, from all official engagements pending the outcome of an investigation into allegations of sexual assault made against him by a foreign female tourist. The emir, who was also barred from travelling, has been confined to the inner chambers of the palace as police took over the premises. Daily Trust gathered that the most senior councillor in the Daura Emirate Council, the Galadiman Daura and District Head of Mai’adua, is expected to assume responsibility for the emir’s official functions and oversee the affairs of the traditional institution during the period of his suspension. The tourist, who identified herself on Instagram as @beduinqa, had alleged in a video that went viral on Sunday that the 92-year-old monarch fondled her hand and other body parts during a visit to the palace as part of her tour of Nigeria. The woman explained that despite cautioning the monarch, he persisted, beaming with smiles. She said although the incident occurred on November 14, she chose not to make it public until she had completed her tour and left the country. The video has elicited reactions, with Amnesty International Nigeria and prominent voices in the North calling for a thorough probe into the act. In a statement on Tuesday by the Katsina State Commissioner for Information and Culture, Bala Salisu Zango, Governor Dikko Umaru Radda expressed displeasure over the emir’s alleged conduct and constituted a committee to investigate the allegation and advise the government accordingly. “Meanwhile, the state government has also suspended all official engagements and travels of the monarch. The government wishes to assure the public that justice will be served and that the outcome of the committee’s findings and recommendations will be fully implemented. “Therefore, the government wishes to call on the general public to be calm, law-abiding and continue with their normal activities,” the statement added. Sources told Daily Trust that the government’s action followed a closed-door meeting involving the Katsina and Daura Emirate Councils as well as other traditional title holders at the Katsina State Foundation Conference Hall on Monday. It was gathered that the Emir of Daura was absent from the meeting. Although details of the deliberations were not made public, there were speculations that the meeting discussed issues affecting the two emirates, including the controversy surrounding the monarch. An activist, Aminu Ibraheem, described the state government’s decision to constitute an investigative committee as appropriate, saying it would help douse the tension generated by the allegation. item.title: No missing funds in $2.04bn Duke Oil crude cargoes — NNPC
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) has dismissed reports alleging that $2.04 billion realised from crude oil cargoes lifted by Duke Oil Company Incorporated, now NNPC Trading S.A., was unaccounted for, insisting that all transactions were fully reconciled. The company said the $2.04 billion represented the gross value of 29 cargoes whose proceeds were set off against the cost of refined petroleum products supplied to Nigeria under the Direct Sale Direct Purchase (DSDP) programme. In a statement by its Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odeh, NNPC said the absence of separate dollar receipts for some cargoes did not indicate missing funds. “No separate receipt appears because the crude sale proceeds were set off against the product purchase price, as the contracts provide,” it stated. Under the DSDP programme, participating traders lifted crude oil in exchange for refined petroleum products, including petrol, for the Nigerian market. NNPC explained that while crude was priced in dollars, products supplied were sold in naira, with transactions reconciled and captured in the audited financial statements of the relevant entities. The company said all 59 cargoes referenced in the reports were accounted for, adding that 30 were paid for in dollars, while proceeds from 28 cargoes, valued at approximately $1.96 billion, were remitted in naira to the NNPC Group Treasury or NNPC Upstream Investment Management Services accounts. The remaining cargo, a February 2023 Bonga tax-oil lifting valued at about $75.9 million, was paid into the then designated Federal Inland Revenue Service dollar account. On Duke Oil’s ownership, NNPC said it was incorporated in 1989 as its wholly owned trading subsidiary, adding that the relationship was documented in its corporate history, audited financial statements and NEITI’s 2023 industry report. It maintained that transactions between the company and its subsidiaries were disclosed as related-party transactions under International Financial Reporting Standards. NNPC reaffirmed its commitment to transparency and accountability, but warned that it reserved the right to take legal action against publications it considered false or misleading. item.title: Delta Killings: Police summon Omo-Agege, Egbo, others for questioning
item.description: *Thugs disrupted preparations, attacked Omo-Agege’s supporters, eyewitness insists By Clifford Ndujihe, Politics Editor The police yesterday summoned former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, Ughelli North Local Government Area Chairman, Jaro Egbo and others for questioning over the political violence that erupted during a campaign rally of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, in Uduere community, Ughelli North LGA of Delta State on Monday. The violence has triggered fresh accusations of political intimidation, police bias and inflammatory rhetoric ahead of the 2027 general elections. While the NDC yesterday boycotted a security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, IGP, Olatunji Disu, accusing the police of failing to protect its members, the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, called on President Bola Tinubu to renounce what it described as dangerous political rhetoric. On a day that supporters of the camps staged protest and counter protest over the killings in Ughelli, Delta State governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, who visited the troubled community, condemned the killings and directed security agencies to track down and arrest those responsible. The state government also imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area. The attack occurred on Monday during a political campaign event involving former deputy president of the Senate and NDC Delta Central senatorial candidate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege. Four persons were confirmed dead, while the NDC said no fewer than 15 others were receiving treatment in intensive care. The Inspector-General of Police subsequently ordered an immediate, impartial and evidence-based investigation, including an examination of the circumstances surrounding the shooting and the conduct of police personnel deployed to the venue. However, Vanguard gathered that one of the four supporters of Omo-Agege, killed in the attack, identified as Efemena Umukoro, had his first child barely six months ago. Yesterday, conflicting casualty figures trailed the killings. with rival political camps claiming seven deaths, against six acknowledged by Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and the police. Ughelli North Chairman, Chief Jaro Egbo, who hails from Uduere, named three persons he said were killed on his side, including the community’s President-General, PG, Cosmos Ejovwoke. Former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, on the other hand, listed four members of his campaign organisation died. The competing accounts bring the number of claimed fatalities to seven, although the governor and police put the toll at six, pending investigations. This was as former Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Olukayode Ariwoola, retd., warned against a repeat of the deadly violence that followed the 2011 general elections, which claimed over 800 lives, urging political parties, security agencies and other stakeholders to take urgent steps to protect the 2027 electoral process. item.title: South-East 400-km $100m gas pipeline, recipe for region’s industrial growth — SEDC
item.description: By Chinedu Adonu For decades, businesses and industries across Nigeria’s South-East region have depended on generators for their daily operations at a high cost. From the manufacturing clusters in Aba, Abia State, to the industrial workshops in Nnewi, Anambra State, the commercial centres of Onitsha, the business communities of Enugu and the productive enterprises of Imo and Ebonyi states, they all face the high cost and unreliability of electricity, forcing them to spend millions of naira to power their generators just to ensure that they remain in business. It has not been easy for a region whose economic strength is deeply rooted in entrepreneurship, manufacturing, commerce, and small-scale industries. Indeed, the energy challenge remains a major obstacle to industrial expansion as they spend huge resources powering their factories. All of them, including small businesses, struggle with rising operational costs. Will the proposed 400-kilometer South-East Gas Distribution Pipeline Project, with an initial investment budget of approximately $100 million, be a game changer for them? This initiative by the South-East Development Commission, SEDC, is planned to connect natural gas resources around the region to industrial and commercial centres across the five states in the region. It was unveiled at the South- East Gas Infrastructure Investment and Project Development Ceremony in Enugu on October 27, 2026. The initiative is a partnership between SEDC and GasSync Limited, NNPC Gas Marketing Limited and other stakeholders. President Bola Tinubu, represented at the ceremony by the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt., Hon. Benjamin Kalu, described the project as an important step towards addressing the infrastructure deficit which has constrained the productive capacity of the South-East region. “There is a sound familiar to every manufacturer in Aba, Nnewi, Onitsha, Enugu and across the South-East. It is the sound of a generator,” Tinubu noted, adding that the resilience of South-East entrepreneurs should no longer be an excuse for inadequate infrastructure. “Our manufacturers should not have to spend more on generating electricity than on expanding production. Our young entrepreneurs should not find that the greatest obstacle to their ambition is the cost of keeping their machines running,” he pointed out. According to the President, Nigeria’s natural gas resources should be measured not merely by what lies beneath the soil but by the factories they power, the jobs they create and the prosperity they bring. A 400-km economic corridor At the heart of the initiative is a proposed regional gas distribution network designed to connect the Assa North-Ohaji gas processing project in Imo State to major industrial and commercial centres across the South-East. item.title: Political Violence: Dying for nothing as a Nigerian politician?
item.description: By Jide Ajani From the First Republic to the Fourth, politicians have been murdered, opposition figures silenced and political supporters killed. Yet, beyond the initial outrage, Nigeria has perfected the art of forgetting its dead. What, then, is the value of dying for a political cause in a country that cannot even preserve the memory of its political martyrs? The alleged assassination attempt on the former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, two days ago, in Uduere community of Ughelli North LGA of Delta State, brings this odd reality into focus once again. Worse, many innocent, ordinary Nigerians have lost their lives while supporting or opposing politicians, only becoming part of an unidentified statistical figure. There is something inescapably tragic about dying while politicking in Nigeria. You could spend a lifetime building a political movement, challenging an unjust system, defending an electoral mandate, or fighting for an idea about your country’s future – or just being loud for nothing like a former, two-time state governor from the South West, or a former Rep and Senator from the North Central. You could become a household name, command enormous political influence and acquire a place in the nation’s history. Then, one morning, gunmen arrive, bullets are fired, and your life is terminated. There will be outrage. Condemnations will pour in. Politicians will issue statements, newspapers will publish editorials (like this), civil society organisations will demand justice, and the police will announce investigations. And then, Nigeria happens, and the people move on. The murder will become another entry in the country’s expanding archive of unresolved political crimes. The victim’s name will gradually disappear from public conversations, except when anniversary commemorations provide an opportunity for political speeches. Even the circumstances of the death may eventually become blurred by competing narratives, political expediency and the convenient amnesia of a nation. Is it, therefore, worth dying for Nigeria’s politics? The question intends to interrogate a society that celebrates political martyrs without demonstrating a corresponding commitment to preserving their legacies or establishing the truth about their deaths. On Monday, November 23, 2026, four persons were killed during an alleged assassination attempt on the former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, two days ago, in Uduere Community of Ughelli North LGA of Delta State. Over a dozen were said to have been injured. Mind you, in an outburst of emotive frustration about happenings inthe political sphere, the self-same Omo-Agege had used the phrase ‘ ig and die’. He was to later clarify that he was merely drawing attention to the need for credible elections. item.title: NRS seeks simpler tax rules for creative sector
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) has called for simpler, clearer and business-friendly tax rules to unlock investment opportunities in Nigeria’s creative economy, stressing the need for a tax system that supports innovation, enterprise growth and wealth creation. The Service noted that the emergence of digital business models, intellectual property-driven enterprises and cross-border transactions required regulations that creators, entrepreneurs and investors could easily understand and navigate. Speaking at the just concluded high-level dialogue on taxation and investment in the creative economy during the Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) event in Lagos, Executive Chairman of the NRS, Dr. Zacch Adedeji, described the creative economy as one of Nigeria’s most promising economic assets, noting that it had evolved beyond entertainment into a major source of employment, foreign exchange earnings, investment and economic opportunities. Adedeji who was represented by the Executive Director, People, Stakeholders and Communication, Mr. Obinna Ihedioha, also said that digital platforms had transformed how creative value was produced and commercialised, with entrepreneurs building businesses around copyrights, designs, brands and digital products. He reiterated that tax administration must evolve to accommodate these developments without discouraging innovation or business expansion. “The government needs sustainable revenue to invest in education, security, technology and infrastructure. But how we tax matters as much as what we collect. It shapes whether businesses start, whether investors come, and whether enterprises grow or stay small,” he said. Adedeji added that the new tax laws offered an opportunity to establish a more efficient system through clearer regulations, reduced compliance burdens for small businesses and improved taxpayer support. He identified clarity, understanding and value as essential to effective taxation, stressing that formalisation should provide creative businesses with tangible benefits, including access to finance, contracts, investment, wider markets and legal protection. The NRS, he said, participated in CANEX through a high-level dialogue, an Investment and Tax Advisory Hub for creators and investors, and the Creative Economy Tax and Investment Initiative (CETII), designed to sustain engagement beyond the event. item.title: Edo Police parades security operative for allegedly leaking information to cultists
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY — THE Edo State Police Command said four members of the Edo State Security Corps, ESSC, have been arrested for allegedly leaking information to suspected cultists to enable them evade arrests. The Command’s spokesperson, Eno Ikoedem, disclosed this while parading 16 suspects arrested across the state in connection with various criminal activities. The suspects, Isaac Irú we, Ashem Gideon, Tony Okhiale and Venture Uzu were arrested at Evbhomore community, in Ovia North-East Local Government Area of the state. They were accused of leaking information on police movements to cultists, enabling them to escape arrest. According to the Command, operatives of the Anti-Cultism Unit acted on intelligence on cult initiation activities in Benin City and immediately swung into action. “Upon getting there, we discovered that someone was giving out information on our movement to these cultists who escaped arrest. “Further investigation revealed that these men are members of the Edo State Security Corps, and four of them have been arrested and they are in our custody.” The command said investigation was still ongoing to ascertain their roles in the secret cult organisation. item.title: Petrol imports crash 52% as crude, wheat top Lagos ports
item.description: By Godwin Oritse Imports of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), also known as petrol, through Lagos ports plunged by 52.23 per cent in November, while crude oil and bulk wheat ranked among the leading commodities imported through the ports in October and November. According to the Shipping Position document obtained from the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), PMS imports fell to 73,895 metric tonnes in November from 328,231 metric tonnes recorded in October. Crude oil imports through Lagos ports also dropped sharply, with 702,254 metric tonnes recorded in October, while no crude oil import was recorded in November. Bulk wheat ranked among the major commodities imported through Lagos ports during the period, with a combined 461,190 metric tonnes recorded in September, October and November. The breakdown showed that wheat imports rose to 252,348 metric tonnes in October and declined by 17.24 per cent to 208,842 metric tonnes in November. Other commodities on the import chart included 402,126 metric tonnes of PMS, 209,000 metric tonnes of Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), or diesel, 212,700 metric tonnes of bulk sugar, 150,000 metric tonnes of aviation fuel and 114,263 metric tonnes of bulk salt. Bulk sugar imports stood at 109,350 metric tonnes in October and 103,400 metric tonnes in November, while bulk salt imports rose from 33,000 metric tonnes to 81,263 metric tonnes over the same period. The document also showed that 624 trucks, 157 transformers and three Rubber-Tyred Gantry (RTG) cranes were received through Lagos ports during the period under review. item.title: Osun man tortures 21-yr-old son to death over N75,000, phone
item.description: By Shina Abubakar Osogbo —The Osun State Police Command has said it arrested a 48-year-old man, Ogunniran Kayode over alleged murder of his son, Raphael, at Faaji, Odo-Otin Local Government Area of the state. A statement by the command’s Public Relations Officer, Abiodun Ojelabi, yesterday, stated that the police received intelligence on October 19, 2026, that the suspect tortured his 21-year-old son to death. Then he buried his body in a shallow grave. Following the intel, the statement disclosed that the operatives of the command swung into action and arrested the suspect as he confessed to the killing of his son. “During the interrogation, he stated that his son stole a sum of N75,000 and absconded with one android phone he bought for him on easy buy to an unknown place. “And being a member of Iru-Ekun Security Network, he was able to get the son arrested through the help of his colleague.” “The case was then transferred to Homicide Section for further investigation”, the statement added. Meanwhile, operatives of the homicide unit visisted the crime scene and the shallow grave, where details and pictorial evidence of the torture were retrieved. The state Police Commissioner, Ibrahim Zungura, therefore, warned individuals with criminal intent to desist from the act or face full wrath of the law. item.title: Political Signals: The Price Of Participation
item.description: Deadly violence in Delta sharpens the question of campaign safety, while economic policy and electoral preparations face tests. An election campaign should ask citizens for their votes. In Uduere, Delta State, families are now mourning people who went to a political gathering. Police said on Tuesday that six people died in Monday’s violence at a campaign event in Ughelli North. That preliminary figure is higher than the four deaths initially reported by Ovie Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation. The circumstances and responsibility remain under investigation. This is the most consequential political development since Friday. Its significance extends beyond one party’s campaign. Every attack raises a question for the next person considering attending a meeting, volunteering or accompanying a candidate: is participation worth the risk? When citizens begin making that calculation, electoral competition has already suffered. Delta Needs Evidence And Accountability Delta Governor Sheriff Oborevwori The NDC has alleged official complicity. The Delta State Government has rejected attempts to link Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to the violence, condemned the killings and promised that those responsible will face justice. Those competing positions must remain distinct from investigative findings. The state has imposed a daily 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. curfew across Ughelli North. Restoring calm is an immediate necessity. Establishing responsibility is the next obligation. The investigation should establish the sequence of events, identify those who used weapons and examine allegations about the conduct of officials and security personnel. Witnesses need protection, and the public needs credible updates. Political leaders also have an immediate responsibility to restrain inflammatory claims and prevent retaliation. The standard is straightforward: lawful political activity must receive protection regardless of the party organising it. A Separate Court Decision Changes The Delta Contest On Tuesday, the Federal High Court in Warri nullified Omo-Agege’s nomination as the NDC’s Delta Central senatorial candidate and directed INEC to remove his name. Reporting attributes the decision to failures concerning the party’s membership register and nomination requirements. Responses from Omo-Agege and the NDC were unavailable in the initial reports. The ruling and Monday’s violence are separate matters. Their proximity establishes no connection between them. Ovie Omo-Agege Electorally, however, the judgment creates fresh uncertainty around an influential politician and the organisation supporting him. Any subsequent appeal, interim order and INEC action will matter. The wider lesson reaches across party lines: recruitment and defections must be supported by lawful nomination procedures. Political prominence cannot resolve defective paperwork. item.title: Nigeria Is Cutting The Budget, But Not The Deficit
item.description: The economic signal this week is that the Federal Government has acknowledged that its 2026 budget is larger than it can credibly implement. President Bola Tinubu has asked the National Assembly to repeal and re-enact the 2026 Appropriation Act, reducing total expenditure from ₦68.323 trillion to ₦65.176 trillion, a cut of approximately ₦3.15 trillion, or 4.6 per cent. Budget revision is not inherently a sign of failure. Governments should adjust spending plans when revenue, financing conditions or obligations change. An unrealistic budget does not become credible merely because it has been signed into law. The more important signal is what remains unchanged: a ₦31.457 trillion fiscal deficit and planned new borrowing of ₦29.218 trillion. Nigeria is reducing expenditure, but it is not reducing the gap between what government earns and what it intends to spend. What Is Being Revised Under the proposed framework, projected federal revenue, including receipts from government-owned enterprises, stands at ₦33.720 trillion. Capital expenditure is estimated at ₦26.232 trillion, while the deficit remains equivalent to 5.64 per cent of GDP. The borrowing plan comprises ₦18.428 trillion in domestic financing and ₦10.790 trillion from external sources. The government says its proposed $7.7 billion foreign loan will fund an existing external-borrowing provision rather than increase the approved envelope. President Bola Tinubu signed into law the Appropriation (Amendment) (No.4) Bill, 2025, on September 30, 2026. The administration says the revision will regularise expenditure incurred by NNPC Limited on behalf of the Federation, address debt-service obligations that were underprovided for, recognise already issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments, and refund ministries and special accounts. Some new allocations are also proposed for critical roads, agriculture, farm productivity, market access and water security. These may be legitimate obligations. But their late recognition exposes weaknesses in the original budget’s preparation. The Credibility Problem The 2026 budget began as an executive proposal of approximately ₦58.47 trillion. It was subsequently expanded and signed at ₦68.323 trillion in April. Seven months later, the executive is asking Parliament to reduce it. The new figure remains ₦6.7 trillion above the original proposal. This sequence matters because Nigeria’s budget has become less a binding financial plan than a collection of ambitions, negotiated additions and subsequent corrections. Ministries receive large appropriations but often wait months for releases. Projects are announced without complete financing. Unpaid obligations accumulate and eventually return as supplementary provisions. A smaller, executable budget would be preferable to a larger one that exists chiefly on paper. item.title: 2027: Omo-Agege Not A Threat, Can’t Get 25% Of Votes For Obi – Delta Council Chairman
item.description: The Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Council in Delta State, Jaro Egbo, has dismissed former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege as a political threat ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that the former lawmaker lacks the support to secure significant votes for the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the state. Egbo said Omo-Agege would struggle to deliver even 25 per cent of the votes for the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, arguing that his political influence in Delta State was exaggerated. The council chairman spoke on Tuesday as a guest on Channels Television’s ‘Politics Today’, where he was asked whether Omo-Agege’s claim that the APC could not win elections in Delta State was a source of concern, particularly given Obi’s victory in the state during the 2023 presidential election. Responding, Egbo questioned Omo-Agege’s political strength, recalling that the former deputy senate president was a member of the All Progressives Congress during the 2023 elections but could not secure 25 per cent of the votes for President Bola Tinubu in Delta State. “When Peter Obi contested and won in Delta in 2023, Omo-Agege was in APC. Omo-Agege couldn’t get 25 per cent of the vote for Mr President. If he was that popular, why was he unable to get 25 per cent for Mr President?” he asked. ﻿ Egbo, who said he belonged to the Peoples Democratic Party at the time, added that his party secured more than 25 per cent of the votes for its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar. He argued that Omo-Agege’s defection to the NDC would not translate into electoral gains for Obi, insisting that the former deputy senate president lacked the political following to influence the outcome of the election. “Now that he has gone to NDC, I am sure he won’t be able to also get 25 per cent for Peter Obi. So, he’s not a threat to anybody. He knows that he’s not a threat,” he said. Egbo, who is also from Ughelli North, Omo-Agege’s hometown, urged Omo-Agege to face the electorate rather than make claims about his political strength, saying voters would determine his popularity at the polls. Egbo also called on the former deputy senate president to tone down his political rhetoric. Omo-Agege had, during an appearance on Politics Today on Monday, dismissed the APC’s chances of winning elections in Delta State in 2027, citing Obi’s popularity and the support base he claimed to command. “Peter Obi remains very popular here in Delta State. There is no chance that APC will win anything,” he said. Omo-Agege, who left the APC for the NDC in May 2026, also argued that a combination of his political support base and Obi’s popularity would make it difficult for the ruling party to win in the state. However, the Federal High Court in Warri, Delta State, on Tuesday invalidated Omo-Agege’s nomination as the NDC candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 elections over alleged violations of the Electoral Act.
